subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- November 17, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - November 17, 2026

Development continues at a steady pace with two significant AI-focused features landing in the PRJCTNatalie repository. The local-ai-deploy branch now includes hardware detection and deployment capabilities via llama.cpp, making it easier for users to run AI models locally on their AcreetionOS systems. Meanwhile, the foundation-scaffold branch has established the groundwork for the Natalie AI agent, which promises to bring intelligent assistance directly into the desktop experience.

Our infrastructure improvements are equally noteworthy this week. The Calamares configuration for Wayland has been updated to force Wayland sessions as the default desktop environment, reflecting our commitment to modern display protocols. A new firefox-fix package has been introduced to restore window position persistence on Linux, addressing a long-standing annoyance for browser users. The initial commit of acreetion-surf v2.0.0 also marks a major milestone for our custom web tooling.

In broader community news, the Manjaro Project has officially established itself as a non-profit organization under German law as Manjaro Project e.V. This structural change provides long-term stability and governance for one of Arch's most popular downstream distributions. Frank Vandermeiren's announcement on the Manjaro forums details how this will protect the project's independence and community-driven ethos for years to come.

The Linux kernel ecosystem saw the release of the 7.4-rc3 prepatch, which Linus Torvalds described as fairly normal with driver updates across networking and other subsystems. Security updates have also been issued across multiple distributions including Debian and Fedora, covering packages from kernel modules to PostgreSQL and network managers. Staying current with these upstream changes remains a priority for our build pipeline.

For users exploring the new Wayland-default experience, remember that XLibre compatibility is maintained for applications that have not yet migrated. The transition has been smoothed by our Calamares customization work, which handles session selection automatically during installation.
